source_text:
Σεμνοπρεπῶς προσαρμόττει τῷ Πνεύματι, ξεναγεῖ εἰς τὸν παράδεισον, εἰς τὴν
οἰκείαν ἀποκαθίστησι νομήν. ∆ιὸ καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς ἔλεγεν· ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ὁδὸς καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια καὶ ἡ ζωή.
thought_title: Christ's manhood joins, guides, and restores; then Christ's own saying
orientation: Eustathius is describing what the manhood of Christ does for believers, then introduces Christ's saying from John 14:6.
pass_a_gloss: In a fitting manner he joins to the Spirit, he leads as a guide into paradise, he restores to the proper pasture. Therefore Christ also said: I am the way and the truth and the life.

choices.why: The adverb describes the dignified appropriateness of the manhood's action; 'fitting' keeps the sense of propriety without overloading it.
The verb means to fit or attach one thing to another; 'joins' preserves the active, transitive force with the Spirit as the object.
The verb specifically means to act as a guide for strangers or visitors; the rendering keeps the guiding action explicit.

choices.english: he restores to the proper pasture
choices.why: The adjective 'proper' marks the pasture as belonging to them; 'restores' keeps the prefix's force of returning to a prior state.
rejected: he re-establishes in their own pasture
he brings back to the fitting pasture

choices.why: The connective marks the saying as a consequence of the preceding description; 'also' renders the καί.

bible_refs.note: ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ὁδὸς καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια καὶ ἡ ζωή

pass_b_english: Christ's manhood joins us fittingly to the Spirit, guides us into paradise, and restores us to our proper pasture. Therefore Christ also said, “I am the way and the truth and the life” (John 14:6).

last_rejected.quote: He joins us fittingly to the Spirit
last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'the manhood of Christ' as subject, not 'He'; ambiguous referent.
last_rejected.fix: The manhood of Christ joins us fittingly to the Spirit, guides us into paradise, and restores us to our proper pasture.
last_rejected.ruling: Greek προσαρμόττει has no explicit subject; 'He' is grammatically valid. No glossary term violated here.

problems.quote: He joins us fittingly to the Spirit
problems.why: Unclear whether 'He' is Christ or the manhood; antecedent ambiguous.

edits.old: He joins us fittingly to the Spirit
edits.new: Christ's manhood joins us fittingly to the Spirit

problems.quote: the covering according to the manhood
problems.why: Same concept rendered four ways; reader may miss they are identical.

variants.text: the covering according to the manhood
the covering that belongs to his manhood

problems.why: Unclear if Eustathius quotes himself from earlier or cites Scripture independently.
problems.fix: Clarify this is a repeated quotation for emphasis.

fixed: The glossary problem about 'the covering according to the manhood' does not appear in the current English text; the English already uses 'Christ's manhood' consistently, so no edit is needed.
The speaker problem is addressed by adding 'again' to indicate that Christ's saying is a repeated quotation for emphasis.

problems.quote: the covering according to the manhood
problems.why: Four variants for same concept may confuse reader into thinking distinctions exist.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'manhood of Christ' or note equivalence.

variants.text: the covering according to the manhood
the covering that belongs to his manhood

problems.why: 'Again' implies prior quotation in original, but fragment order is editorial; reader may think something missing.
problems.fix: Note that 'again' reflects source text, not this arrangement.
